why: All three checks pass; nothing refutes the finding. (1) VERBATIM: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md` (933 lines, fetched 2026-08-02) line 547 reads in full: "Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation. The skill content becomes the prompt that drives the subagent. It won't have access to your conversation history." The quoted sentence is the first of three on that line and the two that follow reinforce rather than reverse it. The other three fields are in the frontmatter reference table: `:271` `background` — "Only applies with `context: fork`. Set to `false` to wait ... Default: `true`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later."; `:272` `hooks` — "Hooks scoped to this skill's lifecycle."; `:274` `shell` — "Shell to use for !`command` and ```! blocks in this skill. Accepts `bash` (default) or `powershell`." The claimed behaviour is accurate on every field, including the v2.1.218 default. (2) CITED LINE: packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:246 declares `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` and :247-:250 carry the four mappings word for word as claimed ('skills do not run in a forked subagent context here'; "it only applies with 'context: fork', which is not implemented"; 'per-skill hook scopes are not implemented'; 'inline shell blocks always run under bash'). The in-file comment block at :223-:245 states the reasoning, so the finding does not misrepresent our state. (3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — the consequence was verified separately from the identifier. Down: the map's only consumer is validation.ts:352, which emits an author-facing WARNING from `skill_validate`; nothing else reads it. `rg -na` across packages/ and apps/ finds no read of a skill-frontmatter `context` key anywhere — not in packages/shared/src/skills/{types,storage}.ts, not in packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts, not in the Claude plugin format adapter (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts maps no skill `context`). Up: the sibling-subsystem trap is present and does NOT rescue the row. This repo does have a fork mechanism (`FORK_AGENT_NAME = 'fork'`, packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:208; R29a/R29b, docs/architecture/fork-subagents.md, /subtask), but it is the Agent-tool/`/subtask` conversation fork that INHERITS the parent conversation — the opposite of skills.md:547's fresh, history-less subagent — and no skill frontmatter routes into it. The neighbouring `agent` field IS implemented, which is exactly why the group looks supported, but base-agent.ts:2540 `applySkillInvocationGrant` uses it as an agent CEILING on the invoking turn (`setSkillInvocationAgentCeiling`, throws 'Invoked skill agent unavailable'), not as skills.md:270's fork target. So the consequence holds: a SKILL.md carrying `context: fork` is expanded inline into the main conversation with full history, where Claude would run it as an isolated subagent. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 — none of the nine concerns skill frontmatter. It is, however, a recorded deliberate decision one level down: worklist §5 U-E asked for 'warn instead of allowlist' and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-e.md:9 and :125-:138 record the ruling **warn** (commit 55b711ce), with `hooks` and `background` already costed and deliberately not half-built in R30c. That makes the gap deliberate and documented — which the finding already says — but not closed, and not a §3 do-not-fix entry. Not a Nessy product difference either: no subscription flow, gateway or rebranding is involved. Only wording quibbles: the fields are not 'parsed' into anything (SkillMetadataSchema is .passthrough(); they are warned about and dropped), and 'behaviour inversion' overstates it slightly — dropping the field yields the same inline behaviour a fieldless skill would get, so the divergence is a missing isolation guarantee rather than an inverted one.
correctedState: Confirmed with two wording corrections. `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` (packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:246-251) lists `context`, `background`, `hooks` and `shell` with exactly the four reasons quoted; its only consumer is validation.ts:352, which turns each into an author-facing WARNING from `skill_validate` ("'<key>' is a documented field this runtime does not implement — it will be ignored"). The fields are not parsed into any runtime value — SkillMetadataSchema is `.passthrough()` — and no code anywhere reads a skill-frontmatter `context`. The repo's `fork` (FORK_AGENT_NAME, definitions.ts:208; /subtask, R29a/R29b) is a conversation-INHERITING Agent-tool fork, the opposite of skills.md:547's history-less subagent, and no skill frontmatter routes into it; the neighbouring `agent` field is implemented as an agent ceiling on the invoking turn (base-agent.ts:2540), not as skills.md:270's fork target. Consequence: a skill setting `context: fork` is expanded inline into the main conversation with full history instead of running isolated — a missing isolation guarantee (same as a fieldless skill), which is more precise than calling it a behaviour inversion. Deliberate and recorded at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-e.md:9,:125-138 (ruling **warn**, commit 55b711ce; `hooks`/`background` costed in R30c) — but not one of the nine §3 owner decisions, so the gap is open, not closed.
